# Shepherd of Hermas Chapter 10 — The EMET Bible (Literal)

**Translator:** EMET | **Source:** Codex Sinaiticus (ch 1-31) / P.Mich. 130 (ch 32+), Shepherd of Hermas 10 | **Source Image:** source-texts/greek-EC/SHE_010_page_001.jpg

---

## Vision 3, Chapter 2

**1** The tower was being built upon a great rock that was square. The rock was more ancient than the world. The tower was built upon this rock. **2** Now the rock and the gate were newly hewn. Six men, youthful, strong, and all alike in appearance, were building the tower. **3** Many thousands of other men were bringing stones for the building — some from the sea and some from the dry land. **4** The ones from the sea were polished and square; but those from the dry land some were square, some were round, some were smooth, some were rough. Some of the round ones were fitting into the building; others were not fitting at all. **5** There were six young men superintending. And I, standing up, watched how the building of the tower was progressing. **6** And I saw that the tower was being built in a solid and beautiful fashion. Seven women stood around the tower, of whom the first was courage; the second self-control; the third power; the fourth long-suffering; the fifth simplicity; the sixth innocence; the seventh purity. **7** Of all these, the first — the most strong — was girded and acted like a man. The others, holding hands with one another and going round in a circle, danced around the tower.

---

*EMET note: The seven women = the seven virtues. The tower is now explicitly set on the primordial rock — likely the pre-existent Christ or the divine Word. The rock "more ancient than the world" echoes the Wisdom theology of Prov 8.*
